hypothesis: A segment values more context than a standard highlights itinerary
test_method: Manual review coding and concept test
evidence_discovered: Article 03 triangulation: walking is a major visitor activity and contextual/hidden-gem supply exists, but preference for richer context over standard highlights remains untested. Article 04 VOC coding repeatedly values contextual storytelling, guide knowledge, hidden/local discovery and information depth; secondary review evidence supports the direction but does not replace primary interviews.
product_implication: Concept format remains open; test visitor preference

hypothesis: A smaller-group or private format improves experience enough to support its cost
evidence_needed: Group-size complaints; price evidence; willingness to pay
evidence_discovered: Small/private formats exist in frozen supply; Article 03 finds no primary willingness-to-pay or experience evidence, so the value premium remains untested. Article 04 reviews repeatedly value small-group interaction and ease of questions; willingness to pay for smaller groups remains untested.
product_implication: Capacity remains open; separate group price from per-person price

hypothesis: A route can create value beyond the highest-pressure central areas
evidence_needed: POIs; mobility; visitor interest; neighbourhood capacity
test_method: GIS review; route walk; stakeholder review
evidence_discovered: City policy favours visitor dispersal and six neighbourhoods show carrying-capacity pressure; this strengthens the relevance of geography but does not prove a specific route creates value. Article 04 contains positive signals for less-obvious neighbourhood discovery, but no route-level resident or mobility validation. Article 06 identifies four STRONG candidate corridors and Article 07 selects Plantage→Oosterpark only as the default concept corridor because it best supports the traced requirements; physical field and resident/stakeholder validation remain open.
product_implication: Route remains open; do not equate different geography with responsible dispersal

hypothesis: An underserved segment or language can be served with qualified capacity
evidence_needed: Source markets; product languages; guide supply
evidence_discovered: Foreign visitation is substantial and multilingual supply exists, but no underserved language/segment is demonstrated without Article 04/05 customer evidence. Article 04 public review sample is English-dominant and cannot establish an underserved language segment.
product_implication: Segment remains open; retain exact live-guide versus audio-guide distinction
evidence_to_date: Germany and France are material Amsterdam/Netherlands source markets; frozen OTA observations show less explicit German/French language disclosure than English and multilingual guide feasibility exists. However Article 04 has no governed non-English VOC and no booking/conversion evidence, so underserved language demand is not validated.
decision_rule: Test German and French preference, comprehension and willingness-to-pay against English delivery before declaring a language opportunity.

hypothesis: The concept can reach target margin without unsafe group size or extractive terms
evidence_discovered: Only 12 frozen observations are price-comparable and cost/commission data remain absent; commercial viability cannot be validated.
product_implication: No price approved; implement common price-observation protocol

hypothesis: Local stakeholders can define acceptable operating conditions
evidence_discovered: Municipal policy clearly constrains nuisance and favours positive city contribution; stakeholder acceptance for any proposed operation remains untested. Article 07 translates municipal rules into explicit product requirements and operating controls, but no local stakeholder acceptance is inferred.
